steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan.

Combine flour, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl. Beat brown sugar and butter with an electric mixer in a separate large bowl until smooth. Stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended. Stir banana mixture into flour mixture until just combined.
Pour batter into the prepared loaf pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, about 60 minutes.
Let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Banana Banana Bread
raw_recipe.description: This banana bread recipe makes an incredibly moist, delicious loaf with very ripe bananas for loads of banana flavor. It tastes even better toasted!

video.description: This banana bread recipe is AllRecipes's most popular recipe ever! In this video, Nicole makes a moist and delicious banana banana bread. After mixing the flour, salt, and sugar, combine the mixture with mashed bananas, brown sugar, butter, and two eggs. Transfer the mixture to a loaf pan and bake it in the oven for around an hour. The banana flavor is so sweet and intense that you have to put banana in the name twice!

review.reviewBody: I've made several banana bread recipes here and I always come back to this one, it is a wonderful standard recipe that you can build upon and customize to your liking. A few pointers... This is a DENSE bread, the last one I made I actually weighed on my kitchen scale and it came to just under 2 1/2 lbs! This probably due to the 2 1/3 cups mashed bananas; I generally use about 5 medium size bananas but have used a little as three and it still came out good. If you like a lighter cake or muffin type bread, look elsewhere. Mix the ingredients carefully; I use my mixer to cream the butter and sugar and incorporate the eggs, but for the bananas and flour mixture I use a wooden spoon and mix gently until everything has just come together. I also add about 3/4 to 1 cup of chopped walnuts. 350 degrees for 1 hour, 15 minutes works for me but it is extremely important that I watch where my oven racks are positioned, too high in the oven and the bottom will not bake correctly, too low and it burns before the middle it cooked through. I position my rack one notch lower than direct middle of my oven and it comes out perfectly. Test with a toothpick in several places for doneness so you don't mistakenly hit a banana piece and think it is underdone. I think that's it!
Excellent recipe!! I added 1/2 cup of chopped walnuts and brushed the top with a mixture of 1tbs water and 3 tbs brown sugar for a sweet crunch on top.

A decent, but not outstanding, banana bread. Its best feature, in my view, is that it takes care of an abundance of over-ripe bananas in one fell swoop. (Plan on five good sized bananas) It certainly was moist and dense, but maybe too much so. I'm wondering if the addition of a little more leavening might improve the tight texture and give it more of a crumb. Also, with this large amount of banana, which in itself is sweet, the amount of sugar could easily be reduced by about 1/4 cup or so. I added a teaspoon of vanilla, a half cup of chopped pecans, and baked in a Bundt pan for about 50 minutes. I'm glad to have used all my over-ripe bananas with just one recipe, but this still won't take the place of my favorite banana bread recipe.

Excellent recipe, I did add a dash of cinnamon and a teaspoon of vanilla. I also made it a 2nd time and put it in an 8 x 8 glass baking dish and topped with a crumb topping( 1 cup flour 6 tbs butter, 1 cup brown sugar and a tsp cinnamon.) Next will be crumb topped muffins.

This is by far the best banana bread I've ever made. As per a user suggestion, I added in 1 teaspoon vanilla, 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon to give it a more fall-flavor, but I'm sure it could be left out and still taste amazing. I baked it in a mini multi-loaf pan (with 6 loaves) for 20 minutes and it came out perfect. My husband and 8 year old cannot get enough! A definite keeper.

Very easy & tasty, I add a tsp of Nutmeg and Vanilla, the walnuts were a great added flavor. I also brushed the top with a 1 tsp. water and 2 tsp. Brown sugar that put a perfect sweet crunch on the top.

My favorite thing to do to Banana Nut Bread is to add chopped pecans, lightly sprinkled with Sanding Sugar (King Arthur Baking) to the top AND bottom of the bread. I do so by adding both ingredients first to the bottom of a loaf pan that has been lightly sprayed with Pam, then to the top of the batter just before going in the oven. It offers a lightly sweet and crunchy texture to the already delicious bread. So good!

Great recipe for ripe bananas, I added a banana extra for extra moist bread! Also added a teaspoon of vanilla and 3/4 cup of walnuts! For the top, crumpled a tablespoon of butter into 1/2 cup of brown sugar and a teaspoon of cinnamon, crumpled on top! So yummy

Good stuff. I used dried dates 1:1 instead of bananas. I added 1/4 tsp A/C vinegar. I made cake flour by substituting 1tbsp A/C flour with 1 tbsp corn starch (per cup). I added 1/2 tsp cinnamon. I cut the sugar in half due to the dates being so naturally sweet. I baked it in mini loaf pans at 350 degrees for 25 minutes.

Made this gluten free with Bob's 1 to 1 GF baking flour and 1/2 cup of chopped walnuts. Also added 1 Tsp of baking powder, 3/4 Tsp of nutmeg and 1 TSP of cinnamon. It took 65 minutes at 350 to fully cook. Came out really good and better than other recipes that use 1/2 cup or more of vegetable oil.

I love this recipe and wanted to make it at our place off the grid (no mixer). So I melted the butter and brown sugar in a saucepan and stirred till incorporated, like caramel. I let it cool just a bit before I added the eggs and bananas. I followed the rest of the recipe as written. Sometimes I add vanilla just because so many baked goods recipes call for vanilla. It came out perfect. I now make it the same way at home without a mixer. It's such a great tasting, easy recipe with minimal ingredients. Very moist.

Great recipe. I like that there aren’t many ingredients. I used a glass pan at 350, and it only needed about 30 minutes. I added a dollop of plain lowfat Greek yogurt and some applesauce and vanilla flavoring. I’ll keep this recipe for sure!
This recipe comes out extremely dry. I cooked it for an hour, and should have only cooled it for 40 minutes at the most. I also think adding more banana would make it more moist.

It's very easy to make if you follow the directions. I found that if I left it in for the full hour it got too hard so I leave it in for 30 to 40 minutes, but I washed it like a hawk. As long as you're watching it and you don't let it get too stiff it's wonderfully moist.
Everyone loves this recipe. The extra banana keeps it moist and full of flavout

I followed this recipe to a T and it has to be the best banana bread I ever ate. I seriously would make a fortune marketing this recipe if I sold it in stores. So glad I didn’t throw out the nearly black bananas on my counter! I didn’t have a mixer so I used an immersion blender to blend the wet ingredients but it turned out very well, nonetheless. (OK i didn’t use a mixer, so not followed exactly to a T) I didn’t overmix the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients, simply folded it together until just mixed. The bread was moist and just sweet enough without being overly cloying. I do not regret the 5lbs I must have gained keeping this whole loaf to myself. Will make again!

This is my go to recipe when I want to whip up a delicious banana bread without following a thousand ingredient driven directions haha. This recipe is straight to the point and I love it! I always add a little bit of sour cream to the recipe to accentuate flavors, some cinnamon and chopped walnuts or pecans or whatever nut I have on hand because I live in a chaos lifestyle and I'm all for it lol. This is always so wonderful thank you!

I use over ripe bananas I freeze to use specifically in this recipe when I accumulate 3 or 4 bananas and my sweet tooth is yearning for this easy recipe. I only add a bit of vanilla extract, cinnamon and nutmeg. Soooo good!
